_readme: Golden set for retrieval: for every fault error_taxonomy.py can raise, which KB chunks
the gate SHOULD let through (must_hit) and which it MUST NOT (must_not_hit).
Patterns are case-insensitive substrings matched against the chunk text
(metadata['text']); a pattern counts as hit when any kept chunk contains it.
Picked by hand from the top-14 candidates per (fault, kind) in kb_local_curated_v4
on 2026-09-11 (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, taxonomy query). Chunks in the top-14 that are
neither listed are 'neutral': off-topic filler that costs context space but does not
teach the model something false about this fault.
must_not_hit is the important half: every entry is a chunk the v6 gate actually put
into the context under this fault's label (or sits next to the cut-off), and that
describes a DIFFERENT fault - the model then cites it as if it explained this one.
When the KB is re-curated (v5) wording changes; add the new phrasing to must_hit rather
than replacing, so the same file can score v4 and v5 side by side.

principle patterns added 2026-09-11 (step 1c) when principle retrieval per error was introduced; must_not_hit there = a principle that would REINFORCE this fault (e.g. 'Do not allow the rear knee to contact the floor' under insufficient back knee flexion) or contradict the fix.
